column3: The Hebrew says “I have made you God to Pharaoh,” without an explicit “like.”
The Hebrew names “My hosts, My people” as two coordinated expressions.
The Hebrew repeats the obedience with “so they did.”
Pharaoh asks for a wonder “for yourselves,” preserving the pronominal phrase.
The Hebrew describes the heart as becoming strong rather than using an explicit passive hardening.
The Hebrew says the heart is “heavy” where BSB has “unyielding.”
The Hebrew uses “serve” where BSB has “worship.”
“Vessels” is supplied in BSB; the Hebrew names wood and stones.
The Hebrew says “he” raised the staff without explicitly naming Aaron.
The Hebrew says “to them” without explicitly repeating Moses and Aaron.
The Hebrew names “his house” rather than “his palace.”
